Pluggable database '%s' is not a standby pluggable database.
cause: The specified pluggable database name was not a standby pluggable database.
action: Provide the correct pluggable database name or container database name and retry.

description: No such pluggable database '%(1)s' at container database '%(2)s'
cause: There was no pluggable database of the given name at the given container database.
action: Provide the correct pluggable database name or container database name and reissue the command.

description: Unable to fetch keystore status of pluggable database %s.
Keystore of pluggable database %s is open.
Keystore password of pluggable database %s is not correct.
Keystore password of multitenant container database %s is not correct.
Pluggable database '%(1)s' already exists(*) in container database '%(2)s'
cause: A pluggable database with the given name already exists.
action: Issue the command again with a different pluggable database name.

description: Failed to fetch Data Guard information for pluggable database '%(1)s' at database '%(2)s'
Target pluggable database must be recovering current redo data from source pluggable database '%(1)s' at '%(2)s'.
Failed to switchover pluggable database '%(1)s' at database '%(2)s' to:
Target pluggable database '%(1)s' at database '%(2)s' has not applied all redo; cannot complete role change
cause: The target pluggable database had not applied all the redo.
action: Wait for the target pluggable database to apply all the redo and try the command again.

description: New source pluggable database '%(1)s' has not registered redo data at database '%(2)s' after switchover
cause: The new standby pluggable database had not received redo data from the new primary pluggable database.
action: Ensure that recovery was started and is running at the new standby pluggable database. If recovery is not running, use the EDIT PLUGGABLE DATABASE SET STATE=APPLY-ON to start Redo Apply and switch logs at the new primary pluggable database.

description: Failed to start recovery for pluggable database '%(1)s' at database '%(2)s'
cause: The operation completed successfully but the attempt to start recovery for the specified pluggable database failed.
action: Please check for any errors in the database alert log and correct them and start recovery using the EDIT PLUGGABLE DATABASE SET STATE=APPLY-ON command.

description: Switchover completed with warnings, new primary is '%s'

cause: The command could not be executed because the specified database was not reachable.
action: Check the network connections to the specified database and reissue the command.

description: Failed to stop recovery for pluggable database '%s'
cause: The command could not be executed because it failed to stop recovery for the specified pluggable database.
action: Please check for any errors in the database alert log and correct them before retrying the command. You can manually stop recovery using the EDIT PLUGGABLE DATABASE SET STATE=APPLY-OFF command and issue the command again.

description: Standby pluggable database '%s' is not applying redo.
cause: Standby pluggable database was not applying redo data.
action: Ensure recovery was started and is running. Use the EDIT PLUGGABLE DATABASE SET STATE=APPLY-ON to start Redo Apply. If this does not resolve the issue, switch logs at the source database.

description: Source pluggable database '%s' must be open in read/write mode for this operation.
cause: The source pluggable database was not open in read/write mode.
action: Open the source pluggable database in read/write mode and retry the operation.

description: Connect identifier does not reference the default service identified by the DB_UNIQUE_NAME initialization parameter, '%s'
cause: The connect identifier referenced a service name that was not the default service name of the member.
action: Oracle recommends that connect identifiers used for Oracle Data Guard use the default service name of the member which is the value specified for the DB_UNIQUE_NAME service initialization parameter.

description: Source pluggable database is '%(1)s' at database '%(2)s'

cause: The source pluggable database was not protected with an active target standby pluggable database.
action: Check the status and connectivity with the target container database.

description: Failover target '%s' cannot recover all redo data; try failover with IMMEDIATE clause.
cause: The command could not proceed because the failover target could not recover all redo data.
action: Issue the command with IMMEDIATE option to immediately convert it to a primary pluggable database.

description: Waiting for '%s' to recover all redo data...
Waiting for redo data from new primary '%s'...

cause: Configuration could not be removed since the primary database contained either an active source or a target Data Guard pluggable database.
action: Retry the operation when there are no active source or target Data Guard pluggable databases.

description: No more standby pluggable databases; stopping redo transport services at source database %s...
Failed to stop redo transport services at database %s.
cause: The operation completed successfully but the attempt to stop redo transport services failed.
action: Use the EDIT DATABASE SET STATE=TRANSPORT-OFF to stop redo transport services.

description: Failed to setup redo transport services at source database %s.
cause: The operation completed successfully but the attempt to start redo transport services failed.
action: Use the ENABLE DATABASE or EDIT DATABASE SET STATE=TRANSPORT-ON to start redo transport services.

description: Waiting for Data Guard broker to initialize.
Data Guard broker did not complete initialization after %s seconds.

cause: An invalid initialization parameter name was specified for the operation.
action: Reissue the command with a valid parameter name.

description: source pluggable database was dropped or unplugged
Failed to update property "%(1)s" for member "%(2)s".
Failed to update parameter "%(1)s" for member "%(2)s".
Warning: DGConnectIdentifer '%s' does not have the same translation on all members.
cause: The specified connect identifier did not translate to the same connect descriptor on all members.
action: Ensure that each member has the same translation for the specified connect descriptor.

description: successfully connected to instance "%(1)s" on member "%(2)s"
failed to connect to instance "%(1)s" on member "%(2)s"
No source pluggable databases at database '%s'
No target pluggable databases at database '%s'

cause: The source pluggable database for this standby pluggable database was dropped.
action: Consider immediate failover to make this a native pluggable database, or remove this standby pluggable database.

cause: The source pluggable database for this standby pluggable database was unplugged.
action: Consider immediate failover to make this a native pluggable database, or remove this standby pluggable database.

description: The source and target container databases cannot be the same.
cause: The specified source and target multitenant container database (CDB) were the same name or same DBID.

description: Source pluggable database "%(1)s" was opened at this instance "%(2)s" to allow ADD PLUGGABLE DATABASE processing, but failed to close it.
cause: Source pluggable database was opened at this instance to allow ADD PLUGGABLE DATABASE processing, but failed to close the source pluggable database.
action: Close the source pluggable database at the instance.

description: Network timeout encountered. Retry the switchover after resolving the network issue.
The standby database "%s" is not using or is not connected to an Oracle ASM instance.
The standby database of the source multitenant container database is using a different Oracle ASM disk group than that of the destination multitenant container database.
The initialization parameter DB_FILE_NAME_CONVERT of the migration destination standby database is not NULL.
The initialization parameter STANDBY_FILE_MANAGEMENT of the migration source standby database is not AUTO.
The multitenant container database %s is not a physical standby database.
The Oracle ASM alias of data file %s is not in the expected location.
cause: In order to reuse the standby database data files during the migration of a pluggable database, the data file should have no Oracle Automatic Storage Management (Oracle ASM) alias, or have its alias located in <DB_UNIQUE_NAME>/<GUID of pluggable database>/DATAFILE.
action: Remove the Oracle ASM alias of the specified data file and issue the command again.

description: A multitenant container standby database in the Oracle Data Guard broker configuration must be specified.
cause: The command did not specify the multitenant container standby database in the Oracle Data Guard broker configuration as being the migration source or destination.
action: Use clause SOURCE STANDBY or DESTINATION STANDBY to specify a standby database in the broker configuration as being the migration source or destination, and issue the command again.

description: Data files cannot be reused when the source multitenant container database is a standby database.
The Oracle ASM alias %s refers to an Oracle ASM file that is not in the expected location.
The guaranteed restore point "%(1)s" was created for multitenant container database "%(2)s".
The guaranteed restore point "%(1)s" was dropped for multitenant container database "%(2)s".
The multitenant container database "%(1)s" failed to find the data file "%(2)s".
The multitenant container database "%s" is in an unstable state.
The multitenant container database "%(1)s" can be restored using the restore point "%(2)s".
Redo apply stopped or failed on multitenant container database "%s".
Copy keystore located in %(1)s for migration destination primary database to %(2)s for migration destination standby database.
Start DGMGRL, connect to multitenant container database %(1)s, and issue command "%(2)s".
If the Oracle Clusterware is configured on multitenant container database %s, add all non-default services for the migrated pluggable database in Cluster Ready Services.
Checking whether standby multitenant container database %(1)s has added all data files for pluggable database %(2)s.
The standby multitenant container database %(1)s failed to add all data files for pluggable database %(2)s.
Waiting for the pluggable database %(1)s to be dropped from standby multitenant container database %(2)s.
Failed to drop the pluggable database %(1)s from standby multitenant container database %(2)s.
The specified file (%s) must not exist.
Fast-start failover lag limit value is greater than fast-start failover threshold value.
cause: The FastStartFailoverLagLimit configuration property is set to a value that is greater than the value of the FastStartFailoverThreshold configuration property.
action: No corrective action is required. Be aware that the primary database will stall after the value of the FastStartFailoverThreshold configuration has elapsed. It will not continue to commit transactions up to the specified lag limit.

description: Unable to fetch keystore mode of pluggable database %s.
KEYFILE and SOURCE IDENTIFIED BY clauses are required.
cause: To migrate a pluggable database with Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) master keys from a standby database, the keys need to be exported to a file and imported from the file at the destination's database. A key file path and the keystore password of the pluggable database to migrate must be provided.
action: Use the KEYFILE and SOURCE KEYSTORE IDENTIFIED BY clauses to specify a key file and the keystore password of the pluggable database to migrate.

description: Exporting master keys of pluggable database %s.
Importing master keys of pluggable database %(1)s to multitenant container database %(2)s.
Environment does not support Data Guard per Pluggable Database.
cause: Data Guard per Pluggable Database command was attempted when the environment did not support it.
action: Data Guard per Pluggable Database operations require two primary container databases in independent, enabled configurations.

description: Removed Data Guard for Pluggable Database setup at %s.
Prepared Data Guard for Pluggable Database at %s.
Enter password for DGPDB_INT account at
Data Guard per Pluggable Database setup is not available.
cause: Data Guard per Pluggable Database command was attempted when the setup was not available.
action: Execute the EDIT CONFIGURATION PREPARE DGPDB command before attempting this operation again.

cause: The per PDB Data Guard pluggable database (DGPDB) setup could not be removed since this configuration contained a remote configuration.
action: The DGPDB will automatically be removed when the remote configuration is removed after all active source and target Data Guard pluggable databases are removed. Alternatively, retry the operation after the remote configuration has been removed.

description: The database must be a primary database or a physical standby database.
cause: The command is failing because the database is neither a primary database nor a physical standby database.
action: This command applies only to databases in the primary and physical standby role.

description: Pluggable database needs to be re-created.
cause: An immediate failover to the active target of this pluggable database caused this pluggable database to require re-creation.
action: Drop this pluggable database. Optionally, create a standby pluggable database for the new source pluggable database.

cause: The length of the output document returned by DBMS_DRS.DGPDB_SHOW() exceeded the internal limit.
action: Query the names of pluggable databases on the multitenant container database using the SHOW PDB command. Then, execute the DGMGRL SHOW PLUGGABLE DATABASE command or DBMS_DRS.DGPDB_SHOW() for each pluggable database.

description: Database must be restarted after creating the server parameter (SPFILE).
cause: The command is being invoked without the WITH RESTART option. Because the database is not using a server parameter (SPFILE), the command cannot complete.
action: Invoke the command again with the WITH RESTART option or after using the server parameter (SPFILE).

description: Database must be restarted after setting static initialization parameters.
cause: The command is being invoked without the WITH RESTART option. Because this command is setting static initialization parameters like DB_UNIQUE_NAME, DB_FILES, or LOG_BUFFER, the command cannot complete.
action: Invoke the command again with the WITH RESTART option or after modifying static initialization parameters as Oracle recommends.

description: Validating database "%s" before executing the command.
Redo transport to '%s' is not valid or has a gap
Pluggable database open in restricted mode.
cause: The pluggable database or its Data Guard partner was open in restricted mode.
action: No action is required. The restricted mode will not prevent a role change. However, it will not be retained after the role change. This is an informational message only.

description: Pluggable database '%s' at container database '%s' is not protected.
Redo apply services of standby pluggable database '%s' is waiting for redo data.
cause: Redo apply services of the given standby pluggable database was waiting for redo data. This could occur if standby redo logs had been added after recovery had been started.
action: Consider switching logs at the source container database to expedite apply at the standby pluggable database.

description: Restricted mode will not be retained after role change

cause: DGMGRL could not connect to the member using the specified connect identifier. This could have happened due to incorrect credentials, listener not running, incorrect listener address or service name in the connect identifier, TNS_ADMIN environment variable not defined or defined incorrectly, the remote member not available, etc.
action: Check the output displayed for the VALIDATE DGConnectIdentifier command for any errors, confirm that the proper credentials were specified and then retry the command.

description: Static connect identifier '%(1)s' does not connect to database '%(2)s'.
cause: The static connect identifier did not allow for a connection to the specified database.
action: Check that the value of the static connect identifier allows for a connection to the specified database. Make any necessary corrections and then retry the command.

description: Current database session was authenticated using operating system credentials.
cause: The current database session was authenticated using operating system credentials, for example, "CONNECT /". If a role change operation was performed, DGMGRL may not be able to connect to the participating databases to complete the role change.
action: Re-connect to the database using an alternative authentication method, for example, database credentials, and retry the command. Note that this will not be an issue if an external passsword store, for example Oracle wallet, is being used and entries have been added to it that specify correct database credentials.

description: This command can only be used for a member that is a far sync instance.
cause: The member that was specified was not a far sync instance.
action: Retry the operation using a command appropriate for the member.

description: This command can only be used for a member that is a Recovery Appliance.
cause: The member that was specified was not a Recovery Appliance.
action: Retry the operation using a command appropriate for the member.

description: This command can only be used for a member that is a remote configuration.
cause: The member that was specified was not a remote configuration.
action: Retry the operation using a command appropriate for the member.

description: This command is not supported for the specified member, "%s".
cause: Either the member does not exist in the configuration, or the command is not supported for the specfied member.
action: Check the member name to see that it exists in the configuration. If it does exist, then use the command that corresponds to the member type.

description: Property "%s" cannot be modified for a Recovery Appliance.
cause: The specified property that corresponded to an initialization parameter cannot be modified for a Recovery Appliance.
action: Specify a different property and retry the command.

description: This command cannot be used for member "%s" that is a Recovery Appliance.
cause: The member that was specified was a Recovery Appliance.
action: Retry the operation using a command appropriate for the member type.

description: This command cannot be used for member "%s" that is a Far Sync Instance.
cause: The member that was specified was a Far Sync Instance.
action: Retry the operation using a command appropriate for the member type.

description: Error: Source primary and physical standby databases have a different number of master keys.
cause: The number of master keys on the primary and physical standby databases were not the same.
action: Do the following on the source physical standby database: 1) Stop redo apply. 2) Close the wallet. 3) Open the wallet. 4) Restart redo apply. 5) Issue "select * from v$encryption_keys" to see all keys on the standby. 6) Retry the MIGRATE command.

description: Member %s disabled, validation will not be performed.
cause: The member specified is disabled, validation of the DGConnectIdentifier cannot be performed.
action: Enable the member and retry the command.

description: Warning: Destination primary and physical standby databases must have the same value for the TDE_CONFIGURATION initialization parameter when Oracle Key Vault is used.
cause: The TDE_CONFIGURATION initialization parameter is set to different values for the primary and physical standby databases when Oracle Key Vault is in use.
action: Set the TDE_CONFIGURATION initialization parameter for the primary and physical standby databases to the same value.

description: Copy the keystore from the migration destination primary database %(1)s to the migration destination standby database %(2)s.
Warning: Current database session was authenticated using operating system credentials.
cause: The current database session has been authenticated using operating system credentials, for example, "CONNECT /".
action: Re-connect to the database using an alternative authentication method, for example, database credentials, and retry the command.

description: Failed to restart Oracle RAC database.
Two or more instances are already running.
Please open the instances that are running and start and open the other instances of database "%s".
Failed to determine the number of instances running, please start all instances of database "%s" to open mode.
Write a message to Data Guard Broker log or process trace file.
DGMGRL command syntax is not recognized.
cause: The command syntax specified is not recognized by the DGMGRL command parser.
action: Use the DGMGRL HELP command to view the command syntax and then reissue the command using the correct syntax.

description: Failover completed with warnings, new primary is "%s".
Primary and standby databases do not have the same number of temp files.
The primary or standby database does not have flashback database enabled.
The primary or standby database does not have its standby or online redo logs cleared.
The primary and standby databases do not have an identical log file configuration.
The primary and standby databases do not have the same settings for their apply-related properties.
The primary and standby databases do not have the same settings for their redo transport-related properties.
Force logging is disabled on the primary database or non-logged blocks were found.
Standby database has one or more data files that are offline.
One or more pluggable databases have save state enabled.
Standby database has one or more pluggable databases that are offline.
Failed to connect to primary database "%s" with connect string "%s" to fetch observer information.
cause: DGMGRL cannot establish a connection to the primary database to fetch observer information.
action: Re-connect to the database using an alternative authentication method, for example, database credentials, or re-connect to the / primary database, and retry the command.
